Thames & Kosmos Remote-Control Machines: Construction Vehicles | Science & Engineering Experiment Stem Kit | Build 8 Real Working Models | Parents' Choice Silver Award Winner |Astra Best Toys for Kids What a toy! Using this kit, it's possible to make 8 different remote control construction vehicles (forklifts, bulldozers, etc,), or experiment and create your own thing. What I think is most impressive is that this kit can be used with children as young as 6 years old, if you believe the ages on the box.

Like all of the times that I've tried to build from the instructions, Daddy had to do most of the work when my daughter lost interest, although she's on the lower end of the recommended spectrum. The kit is easy, but it's not a cakewalk, and I don't think she could have done it on her own, but she did help, and was pleased to play with the result. The remote control aspect really sets this well above most building toys, and now she's asking me to build new stuff for her all the time.

Note that the picture on Amazon is showing "the models" and has 10 images, but the book shows how to create only 8 of those. It is absolutely possible to create your own thing.

I have spent the last 90 minutes trying to decorate this mug. The parts sent with the mug do not attach; you can place them but they immediately fall off. Those parts fit to one another very well, but they decline to play nicely (or at all) with their mug.

I tried LEGO pieces and they do not want to be pressed onto the mug. I really cannot blame them.

The only block pieces that do fit onto the mug are ones I had purchased from Dollar Tree. They meld easily with the mug and hold beautifully. Unfortunately, the only surface that will accept them is the front of the mug. As you can see from the pictures they are holding well, but the rest of the mug surfaces are...well, I am trying so hard not to be all negative and everything, but the mug is so poorly designed and sloppily made that nohting will attach at all, not LEGO, not the mug company's blocks and not even the pieces of white bread that I smushed together and tried to mold to the pegs and holes. It stuck whilst still moist and them fell off when it dried and I picked up the mug to check.

We are a totally dedicated LEGO family. We have even indoctrinated...coerced...um...lovingly brought my son-in-law into the LEGO Love. We give and share those precious bricks at every gifting opportunity. There have been times when my grandchildren are out playing with their friends and my daughter and I are still inside playing. I recently learned that the one set she would love to have is the Friend's Heartlake Hotel, but by that time it was already hovering around $400.00. I am thinking that I will make provisions in my will for her to have one.

Sadly, I bought two of these. Double the heartbreak. Do not buy this unless you are planning to do what I intend to do with them. I have a tiny ton of old costume jewelry that I use for crafting and I am going to use Gorilla Glue to cover the mug with some cool bits and bobs of jewelry. That will be a totally huge and groovy improvement to the really quite pathetic red C that is now on the mug. I am an old granny and am surprised how disappointed I am with this mug.

Please protect your loved ones and buy something else. You can buy some nice real LEGO packs for the $26.00 I wasted on this crap, or a very large amount of blocks and accessories of the blocks sold at Dollar Tree. Tell them I sent you.

Love,
Granny

text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster The recon has always been a pretty good blaster.  Somewhat prone to jamming, and on the short side for range, but accurate as all get out, and good for modding.  Then enter the Retaliator!  This is not your typical Recon with a face lift!  The shell is still recon- but with a new name badge and the digital camo effect.  The GUTS are all new- direct plunger powerhouse.  This blaster will pop the elite darts out to 75 feet (angled shots) and will put darts out to 50 feet level shot.  The accuracy is still there too!  It will take the old Streamlines too(with a noticable loss of range and accuracy)  This blaster will jam- but if your careful to pull the cocking slide back fully (not just till it clicks, but fully back, usually a couple mm beyond the point of the trigger latch engagment) jams are minimal (we actully shot 50 or so shots without a jam!).  I'm not a huge fan of barrel and stock attachments, but these are pretty good on this blaster.  The barrel does reduce range (about 8 to 10 foot lose), but does increase accuracy (we use cardboard standups aprox 2" wide by 4" high and can hit them 8 out of 10 time without the barrel and 9 out of 10 with- at 25 feet).  The new 12 shot clip (mag) is very cool and makes a nice transition between the 6 shot (way to small) and the 18 (nice capacity- but kinda gets in the way).  My daughter uses this blaster to sniper me all the time.  All she needs to see is a foot or a hand sticking out from behind the couch and I'm toast!  All in all a worthy upgrade to the recon.  Great for a primary or secondary carry.  I did take 1 star off because nerf still hasn't made this jam proof- close, but not perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster

City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS) It's fake LEGO. It may pretend it isn't, but it is,
As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!
text_fidelity_b: City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS)

text_fidelity_a:
The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games I'm a wolf lover as well as a game nerd and couldn't pass this one up! It is absolutely beautiful out of the box. I'm impressed they kept it to a $50 price point with the level of detail here, I've seen similar games priced closer to $80!

I haven't had a chance to play yet because I need to get folks together but I did watch a video playthrough about the rules after reading the guide so that I'd be prepared. They are complex but once I watched the video it made a lot more sense. It's definitely tactic-heavy in that you need to change strategy based on what your opponent is doing or what phase of the moon it is on. I love many of the creative points in the design, and I love a game with a very clear endpoint because I hate games that go on forever! 75 minutes is perfect for a game night.

I especially love the design of the wolf cards. They are extremely clear where the tiles and meeples go etc. It's not only attractive but it also includes reminder text which is really helpful for absent-minded players like myself. I love how the rules for your items level up as you get more pieces on the board.

My favorite part about games like this is that it's possible to lose a battle here and there and not feel discouraged halfway through. Since a lot of scoring can happen later, it keeps players invested until the end. This generation of games is so different from the ones before!

My only complaint is that with a game like this it is so easy to lose a meeple because they are so small and so many. This can make it hard to trust strangers with at board-game meetups.
text_fidelity_b: The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games

I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this lounger and I am tempted to buy another just to have an extra in case mine meets with demise (Minnesota winter storage)

Radio Flyer (My 1st 2-in-1 Wagon, Red Is this easy to assemble? Apparently! My 3 little guys put it together while I was cooking supper. So, it's also quick to assemble. They did a great job, minus putting the handle on backwards. Though I've tried to take the wheels off to move the handle around, I've been unsuccessful. That hasn't kept them from having a great time with it, though. My older 2 have pulled my 3 year old around in it, and he has had a great time loading and unloading his stuffed animals. The good news is, even if put on backwards, the handle still locks!

This wagon is on the small side. My 3 year old is small for his age, but he still has to squeeze in there. I wouldn't recommend older than that riding in it due to fearing it will break. It also flips over pretty easily, so I don't recommend too much riding in it, period, especially for the younger little ones. It IS great for pulling things like stuffed animals and books around, though.

This wagon is plastic, like most of the other Radio Flyer toys these days. We have a few of them, and they have always been well loved and played with by my boys. Despite being plastic, they have proved to be very sturdy so far.

Overall, you really can't go wrong if this wagon is for pulling little toys around. It will provide hours of (semi)quiet fun for your little one. If you're wanting something to pull a child around in, though, I'd go a different route.

text_fidelity_a:
Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up Back in the late 1980’s and early 1990’s I used to play MASH in school. No, it had NOTHING to do with the sitcom that some might remember.

The MASH game was an acronym for:

Mansion
Apartment
Shack
House

It was sort of a future/fortune telling game mainly for giggles. The original paper game was of course to tell you what “crush” you ended up with, what kind of “housing” you resided in, what you drove, and how many kids you had. One person drew a circle/swirl, like in this game, and you said STOP to get the “counter” number to begin the fortune telling – crossing off at the count.

This is an updated version of that game, though in all honesty, not near as much fun.

The basic model was to list MASH and three other variables – kids, car – crush. Like this one; you swirled and counted until you came to the end.

This game, while more grown up, is nothing like the old game even with the introduction of “scenarios”. Sadly, this is pretty much paying for something that you can get for free – sometimes you can even add more to the choices – pets, location, job(s) … with the old version, the only limitation is imagination.

This game does pay homage to its origins and includes the ORIGINAL MASH “scenario” card though the choices for everything is left up to the “decks” and not the players’ imaginations. That was, again the entire fun of it.

Depending on exactly what you’re looking for with this game – it might be best to save your money and write it out like I did or look online for MASH game cards. There are really cute printable ones out there.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up

MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS The MACTANO Starry Night Building Kit is a micro brick set, so it’s not compatible with regular size building sets. And the bricks really are micro! I don’t recommend this set for kids or anyone with dexterity issues. Many of the pieces are smaller than the tip of a q-tip.

I’ve been building sets for three decades, and I’ll be honest, this one was a big challenge. Patience and attention to detail are extremely necessary. I keep looking at my finished set and noticing mistakes I made, or steps I missed.

The pieces do stay together, very important for an off-brand set. The kit includes a tiny brick separator, it’s cute and much needed.

If I have so much experience, why did I find this set so difficult? First, each step in the instructions is really 2 to 5 steps. For example, step 12 uses over sixty(!) pieces to put together four rows of the backdrop. Every step is like that, and you have to pay extremely close attention to figure out what pieces go where.

Second, sometimes it wasn’t clear what color to use or where a piece should go, but I couldn’t look ahead. Future steps greyed out the colors for previous steps, and sometimes didn’t show the complete build, part of it would be cut off.

Third, some of the colors are very hard to tell apart. I used the wrong shade of blue multiple times, but I quit caring. Most of the painting is blue, so only I know about those mistakes. But for the very dark blue and very dark green, it’s hard to see the outlines of the individual pieces in the instructions.

I build brick sets to relax. Working on this set was the opposite of relaxing for me, since I had to focus so much.
text_fidelity_b: MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS

I called Hasbro this morning and they are sending a return label, and a different replacement baby alive doll.
Overall I’m extremely disappointed in this product. I was unable to find anyone else having the same issue. I highly doubt it is result of my daughter playing. This is designed for children ages three and up. She is a nine-year-old who is extremely cautious. This was her only Santa gift and it has caused lots of heartache. We do our best to downplay the frustration. We understand malfunctions happen. I just don’t want anybody else to have the same issue and feel alone like we did.
I would not recommend this doll specifically. Fingers crossed the third replacement (A different design) works more than once.

Update: we purchased a 3rd replacement happy hungry baby from a local store. A different hair color than our first two. Hoping it’s a different production line. It’s still working on day two! My daughter squealed this morning with excitement “she works! She works!”

Shes used the 3rd happy hungry baby (brunette) for weeks now- almost daily. Its been working wonderfully! Still unbelievable that the first two were defective (Black hair). Raised to 2 stars for the fact she loves it. The headache and hassle of 2 dolls would make it where i would -cautiously- recommend. Keep the box (and receipt) for at least a month.

Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

text_fidelity_a:
Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors The Alias is potentially a great example of the new generation of quadcopters with electronic flight control boards that provide six axis stabilization. When their transmitter control levers are properly trimmed at the beginning of each flight they will hover very stably and are easy to fly even for a beginner.

Unfortunately, LaTrax and Traxxas (LaTrax makes the product and Traxxas provides all customer support) released the Alias before they found a good quality motor that works properly with the Alias. Since the Alias uses four motors and is inoperable if any one of the motors fails this is a major problem.

My Alias flew great for the first two days, but then it became very unstable and flew unpredictably. After only the the sixth or eighth flight one of the motors failed and the Alias would not fly at all.

Traxxas told me the Alias does fly unpredictably when one of its motors is weakening and getting ready to fail. They said they would send me a free replacement motor, but so far it has not arrived. Looking at other Amazon reviews, and on the internet, I see that many other people have also had very early motor failures. I strongly recommend people should not buy the Alias until LaTrax and Traxxas have figured out the early motor failure problem, presumably by finding a better motor.

Update: January 14, 2014

After two initial days of use before one of the motors broke, I have been unable to fly my new Alias for two and a half weeks now. Traxxas keeps saying they will send me a new motor as soon as the most recent batch they received "gets through quality control". I fear I have wasted $150 to buy the Alias.

Update January 20, 2014

After three weeks Traxxas finally sent me a replacement motor ....drum roll.....however, they sent the wrong motor! Traxxas checked their records, agreed they had sent the wrong motor, and promised to send the correct motor. I am pleased they are trying to provide good customer service, but I am now in my fourth week without being able to fly my otherwise excellent Alias after one of its motors broke on the second day after I opened it at Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors

LEGO Disney Aurora’s Royal Carriage 43173 Creative Princess Building Kit, New 2020 (62 Pieces) Aurora’s Royal Carriage is a great set. It would make a good gift or introduction to Lego for a Disney Princess fan. The set could also fit in with other Disney sets, such as Cinderella’s Castle Celebration (43178), or even the Lego Friends sets, since the mini-dolls are the same size.

The carriage build is quite easy. As usual with Lego, the instructions are clearly explained, and should be doable by 5+.

Aurora’s accessories include two pearl gold crowns (so handy, in case one gets lost), two pink flowers, and an owl minifig. The owl is super cute, too -- I really like his expression.

Elmer's Gue Premade Slime, Slime Kit, Includes Fun, Unique Add-Ins, Party Pack, 20 Count Good value on this party pack. What a unique item. I am familiar with Elmer's Gue and also their packs that you make your own slime. I figured with this pack ... there was enough for me ... and to share with young ones in our congregation that have been mostly homebound during Covid. The 20 pack means there is plenty to go around ... so easy to share.

Usually ... I am sensitive to chemical smells but these do not seem to bother me. Vibrant colors and also clear consistency. Add ins are glitter or tiny foam balls. Yes ... the foam balls might get away from you. Yes ... you might find them here and there in the house. I don't consider that a negative. I consider that crafting. Crafts will always create some sort of mess. Nothing is perfect.

Stretches well. Creates air pockets to pop. Easy to mold. Have had no problems with it drying or molding. We always wash our hands first so as not to make it dirty.

Overall ... I just cannot think of a negative that makes this not worth buying. It has been so much fun and again I love that the pack makes it totally sharable. No regrets.

--------------
* There is just something satisfactory about spinning objects. LOL!

HOW TO CUSTOMIZE:
--------------------------
* Mine did not come with any instructions, but I contacted the sellers and here are the instructions:

Step 1: Twist the top and bottom shell to open the Fidget roulette
Step 2: Remove the Sticker with our logo. (It will reveal a screw)
Step 3: Remove the screw while holding the front dial with the “?” (This will give you access to the Answer Wheel)
Step 4: Go to Fidgetroulette.com , download the Answer Wheel you desire and print it (If you don’t have sticker paper available, you can use regular paper and use paper glue)
Step 5: put it back together and have fun!

THE BAD:
------------

I build on our dining room table but when I have to clean up, I have to put away all the pieces and cover the whole thing with paper or posterboard because my cat sits on it, eats pieces, throws up on it, or tosses pieces to the floor.

I have been looking for a puzzle board/ storage solution for a while and found this one: The medium 1500 piece size is a good size for most of the puzzles that I do. It is sturdy and was packaged beautifully (foam on the back and front and around the corners as well). It arrived perfectly with no issues. This board showcases 6 drawers - 2 different sizes and a plexi cover for the puzzle. While larger, it was easy to move around as long as you don't tilt it (drawers may fall out). I have only really moved it inbetween puzzles, but if you are careful I guess you could move it out of the way, especially with some help and slide it under a couch or bed.

Aside from puzzling, I think this would be a great board to use for boardgames as well especially those with lots of player/playing pieces, because you can house/hide them in the drawers (up to 6 players).

For the cost, it seems a little underdone. The particle board is plain, it is a bit on the heavier side, and there is no felt that you can find on some boards.

Overall, I am enjoying my use of this product. It is getting the job done, especially if you are tormented by a cat like I am.

UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017) This UBTECH JIMU ROBOT-BUILDERBOTS KIT (Interactive Building Block System (357 Piece)) is so beautifully packaged, you’d almost think it was a smartphone or an Apple product. It comes in a heavy-duty, magnetic-closure box that opens like a book. Inside, the main controller, connectors and fasteners are packed in colorful paper boxes that nest perfectly in the big outer box. Is such a lovely unboxing experience wasted on a kid’s toy?

This kit will make either a “Grabberbot” or a “Digbot”. I say “either”, because the building components are extremely hard to take apart--you are NOT going to want to try a rebuild of either completed robot. Some (but not all) of the components are similar to LEGO Technic elements, but they’re smaller and definitely NOT compatible with LEGO.

In an afternoon (about 4 hours), I built the Grabberbot, which I like a lot. Using the Jimu app (iOS or Android), it’s easy to drive, very responsive, and actually picks things up. Grabberbot has a cool, multicolored LED light (you can program custom colors), and he has a voice cube with a large repertoire of sounds (also programmable).

Grabberbot is controlled with Bluetooth--pairing is easy, once he’s turned on or plugged into a power source. He does NOT have a separate controller, so you must have a tablet or a smartphone to make him work. (I use an iPad Mini.) It’s a good idea to charge the controller cube before you start building--it takes an hour or so. You do NOT want to spend an afternoon building a robot, and then have to wait for the battery to charge before you can play with it!

You can’t build the Grabberbot without a tablet or smartphone--you have to download the app to get the building instructions. (This is a pet peeve of mine; I believe that the instructions for building toys belong in the box.) However, in defense of the download-only instructions, they are presented in 3D! If you’re unsure about a particular step, you can rotate the model 360 degrees and look at it from every angle until you’re sure that you’ve got it right.

Grabberbot is more difficult to build than a motorized LEGO set. There are three reasons for this: (1) the instructions don’t always show the elements recognizably or exactly the way they go together (e.g., the sensor box has fewer connector holes than the one shown in the instructions); (2) the instructions don’t always start at the easiest place for the next step in the assembly; and (3) the components click together so firmly, you need pliers to separate some of them if you make a mistake.

Sadly, the color-changing LED light needs to be programmed if you want it to do more than flash colored lights for a few seconds when Grabberbot is first turned on. I did very little with the programming portion of the app, which requires you to identify which of the four servo motors you want to give instructions to (they are numbered), to choose commands for the motor(s), and to name and record the resulting
action. Programming doesn’t seem to be hard, but it does take some study and practice.

There is a charger with an AC adapter included. The red light on the controller box changes to green when the battery is fully charged. A firmware update starts automatically when you first connect the Grabberbot; it takes only a few minutes.
text_fidelity_b: UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017)

text_fidelity_a:
DSS Games The Couples Game That's Actually Fun [A Party Game to Play with Your Partner] If you've ever played or seen the Newlywed game, this should be familiar. Players get a small dry-erase board with markers and eraser, and a card is drawn with a question. The players have to write their answer and reveal them at the same time. Depending on the question, answers have to either match, call out the other player, or be more creative than the other.
The rules aren't clear since points aren't really awarded, and who's to say which answer is more creative for those cards... but winning or losing is not the point of this game- the point is to have FUN! And fun it definitely is! My wife and I played for a long time and really found ourselves laughing out loud.
I'd imagine this game will adapt to the players- if you want a squeaky clean family friendly game, the answers can be totally safe, or if you'd rather answer them in NSFW ways you can choose to. The interpretation of the answer is totally up to the players.
text_fidelity_b: DSS Games The Couples Game That's Actually Fun [A Party Game to Play with Your Partner]

text_fidelity_a:
Asmodee Hit Z Road This is a very silly game, despite the theme. Not a gory or cartoonish zombie game, it really could be almost anything in place of them: Mad Max-style marauders, for instance. What's nice about that is, if you're anything like me, and you're totally over all types of zombie games, you will still be able to play Hit Z Road.

This game is really a push your luck dice rolling game with auctions. You're trying to survive until the end of the road, and you need to make some meaningful choices along the way that could make your journey much easier, or much more daring. There is some player elimination, but it's not one of those "you can die on the first turn" types of eliminations - our earliest death was about 10 minutes before the end of the game.

I think a lot of people will find the artwork on this game to be fantastic, and I have to admit that it is daring, different, and one of the most unique looking games out there. While I can admire the work that went into it, the art just doesn't appeal to me.

The name, by the way, might be one of the worst in the history of board gaming.
text_fidelity_b: Asmodee Hit Z Road

text_fidelity_a: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children This is a fun 4wd car to drive.  It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.
text_fidelity_b: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children
